brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

finish.summary: Low hex shelf unit: three full bases in a row at level 0 with a full base stacked on the middle one, plus two north-half bases in front, each holding a drawer. Bases are joined with joint bolts and the tops have covers. Edges are capped except one, where a cap would hit a drawer frame. check_build shows no errors and meshClash is "clear". The 50 kg rating is not verified, because the configurator checks fit, not strength.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit with surfaces for books
requirements.evidence: Full bases at (-1,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,0) and (0,0,1), plus half bases at (-1,1,0) and (0,1,0). Covers on all 5 top faces make the shelf surfaces. Joint bolts join the level-0 bases.
drawer:0#-1,1#cut and drawer:0#0,1#cut sit on the cut faces of the two half-n bases. The mesh gate is clear.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only, not strength or load. No load rating can be claimed, so 50 kg is not verified. You would need physical load testing or the manufacturer's specs.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear. The only issue is an info note: the edge at 0,1,0;150 has no cap, because a cap there would hit the drawer frame (MESH_CLASH).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
